newsitem.title: USA: CNB seeks better performance, liquidity.
newsitem.headline: CNB seeks better performance, liquidity.

text.p: CNB Bancshares Inc admits that it is an underperforming company, but says it is working to improve its performance while trying to attain liquidity that will make it attractive to institutional investors.
"We are not as productive a company as we ought to be," John Spruill, chief financial officer, said at a Howe Barnes Investments Inc conference here.

The $4.1 billion asset bank holding company, which is based in Evansville, Indiana, had a 1.06 percent return on assets in 1996, well below the 1.25 percent benchmark the bank has set. Its efficiency ratio was 63 percent, less efficient than the 58 percent benchmark the bank is currently seeking.

Spruill said the bank expects to reach a 58 percent efficiency ratio -- the measure of the cost of raising income -- by the end of 1998, though he added that benchmark will likely be moved lower by then.
An improvement to 58 percent efficiency would add about $0.36 a share to annual earnings, he said.
"We're driven to do things about that," Spruill said about improving performance.
Among those things are closing small offices, centralizing support functions, offering early retirement to reduce staff and increasing incentive-based staff.
Spruill said some of the performance problems come from integrating acquisitions, especially thrifts the company has acquired.
CNB currently sells about 2.4 financial products to each household it serves, but has set a goal of four products, he said.
The company is also seeking to improve upon its liquidity of about 9,000 shares traded a day. That level is too low to attract some institutional investors, he said.
CNB shares were unchanged at 37-7/8 Tuesday on volume of 2,200 on the New York Stock Exchange.
